componentA.class: raw Blitz (N0), not a layout_normalize pass: every vellora layer step was 0 at 10-crates (N0 = B0 = L0 = each pass = P = -2 px)
componentA.cause: Blitz 0.3.0-beta.4 has no <table cellspacing> presentational hint, and since beta.4 adds border-spacing at the table edges (layout/table.rs style.gap block: spacing added to the table padding), where the pin 2003ba5 used it as the grid gap only. The outer table's cellspacing="0" kept the UA 2 px: cells inset 2 px per side and 2 px per row (layout-diff N0 dx +2 / -2 px, dy +2 px per row).
componentA.fix: d648e8f (cellspacing as a UA-sheet presentational hint), 14898b9 (cellpadding, same mechanism)

componentB.class: vellora input (pre-N0): the Blitz viewport width; not visible to layout-diff, which lays Chrome's DOM out at vellora's viewport
componentB.cause: vellora truncates the 594.96 pt (793.28 px) A4 content width to an integer viewport (15 mm margins: 679.89 -> 679 px); Chrome's print layout box is ceil(210 mm px - margins) = 681 px with its x origin at round(margin) = 57 px (chrome-print-viewport.json, 10 margins: width = ceil(793.70 - ml - mr), height = floor(1122.52 - mt - mb) in every case). Right-aligned text therefore ends 2 px (1.5 pt) further left than Chrome's in the PDF while N0 = 0 against Chrome's DOM; left-aligned text is off by the 0.31 px origin rounding only.
componentB.pinOnlyMatched: the pin's right-aligned header words matched Chrome by cancellation: the pin's gap-only spacing put the nested table's cells 2 px wider (+2 px) and the viewport put them 2 px left

experiment.change: viewport width = ceil(content width + (210 mm px - 793.28)) (A4 only, measurement hack, reverted)
